answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one operator across a plume of accounts does not multiply influence: every account needs its own capital, and rewards accrue only after verified work. The attacker pays an upfront opportunity cost and risks losing the stake, while honest agents can build reputation without trusting a quill or a polished profile at the ledge.
